title: Monitor Switcher monitor profile
description: Describes how to switch inputs on one monitor model. See docs/adding-a-profile.md.

id.description: Unique, lowercase id: <vendor>-<model>, e.g. lg-32un880. Must equal the file name without .json.

match.description: How to recognise the monitor. Product code wins over capabilities model, which wins over EDID model name.

manufacturer.description: Three-letter EDID PNP manufacturer id (GSM = LG, DEL = Dell, SAM = Samsung, ...).

productCodes.description: EDID product codes as hex strings, e.g. "0x774F". Run `monitorswitcher --list` to see yours.

capabilitiesModel.description: Model token from the DDC/CI capabilities string, e.g. "UN880".

modelNames.description: EDID monitor names. Avoid generic names such as "LG HDR 4K" that many models share.

protocol.description: Protocol id. Built in: mccs-standard, lg-alternative.

id.description: Short id used by the CLI and settings: hdmi1, hdmi2, dp1, dp2, usbc, ...

name.description: Port label as printed on the monitor.

code.description: Value sent with the protocol's command, as a hex string.

verified.description: true once someone has confirmed this code switches the monitor.

retries.description: Extra attempts if the transport reports a failure.

postSwitchDelayMs.description: Pause after a switch before the next command.

ignoresCommandsWhenInactive.description: true if the monitor ignores DDC/CI arriving on an input it isn't showing, so a computer can switch away from itself but not back.
